gaps.sentence: I fell ___ with my best friend over a silly remark.
gaps.explanation: fall out (with somebody) = have an argument and stop being friendly.

gaps.sentence: The new stadium made ___ an impressive sight.
gaps.explanation: make for = produce a particular result (make for a good atmosphere); also move towards.

gaps.sentence: I came ___ an old letter while clearing the attic.
The negotiators refused to give ___ to the hijackers' demands.
gaps.explanation: give in (to) = stop arguing and accept; give up = quit.

gaps.sentence: The old cinema was knocked ___ to build a car park.
gaps.explanation: knock down = demolish a building; hit with a vehicle.

gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: You go ahead; I'll catch ___ with you later.
gaps.explanation: catch up (with) = reach the same point/level as somebody.

gaps.sentence: The hotel was full, so we couldn't check ___.
gaps.explanation: check in = register; check out = leave and pay.
